bill.name: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to “Review of Final Rule Reclassification of Major Sources as Area Sources Under Section 112 of the Clean Air Act” (H.J. Res. 79)
bill.status: Introduced in House · Fedorchak · referred to Energy and Commerce on 2025-03-24 · sponsor introductory remarks on 2025-03-27
bill.analyzed: Full introduced-in-House joint resolution (2 pages; one operative clause), with current H.J. Res. 79 status and enactment of related S.J. Res. 31 checked separately

sourceLimits: The supplied 1,324-byte, 217-word raw source is a flattened extraction of the introduced-in-House version. It contains the resolution's sole operative sentence but has no page boundaries or metadata sidecar and omits the standard resolving formula visible in the matching official PDF; that PDF establishes the two-page count. Congress.gov actions metadata, checked separately, still records H.J. Res. 79 as introduced, with sponsor introductory remarks on March 27, 2025 as its latest action. Congress.gov also identifies S.J. Res. 31 as a related measure and records that it became Public Law 119-20 on June 20, 2025, disapproving the same cited EPA rule with substantively equivalent text. The supplied source identifies that rule by agency, title, Federal Register citation, and publication date but does not reproduce the rule, state findings or a downstream purpose, specify a replacement regulatory regime, create an appropriation or reporting duty, or identify a quantitative outcome. Its only express result is a one-time legal state, and that state was separately produced by the related enacted measure. Treating enactment or the rule's legal status as an outcome series, or writing P(rule has no force or effect | disapproval enacted), would be tautological rather than an empirical forecast. Accordingly, this extraction has one provision and one literal goal and effect, but zero implementation barriers, forecastable metrics, stance matrices, series hints, or conditionals. It does not infer effects on source classifications, emissions, public health, regulated-facility counts, compliance costs, agency workload, or any other downstream outcome.

provisions.title: H.J. Res. 79
provisions.heading: Congressional disapproval of the identified EPA major-source reclassification rule
provisions.quote: That Congress disapproves the final rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to “Review of Final Rule Reclassification of Major Sources as Area Sources Under Section 112 of the Clean Air Act” (89 Fed. Reg. 73293 (September 10, 2024)), and such rule shall have no force or effect.
provisions.context:
H.J. Res. 79 invokes chapter 8 of title 5 and identifies one EPA final rule by title, Federal Register citation, and publication date. Ms. Fedorchak, for herself, Mr. Balderson, and Mr. Allen, submitted the analyzed introduced-in-House version on March 24, 2025, and it was referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce. Its sole operative clause states that Congress disapproves the cited rule and that the rule shall have no force or effect. Congress.gov separately identifies S.J. Res. 31 as a related measure and records that the Senate-origin measure became Public Law 119-20 on June 20, 2025; H.J. Res. 79 itself remains introduced, while its stated legal objective has already been accomplished through that related law.

Source limits / honesty note: The cited EPA rule is not reproduced, and the resolution supplies no findings, substantive replacement rule, implementation steps, quantitative target, reporting requirement, or downstream outcome. The source therefore supports only the express legal objective and legal effect recorded below. It does not support an inference about source classifications, emissions, public health, regulated-facility counts, compliance costs, or agency workload. The binary legal consequence is a one-time policy state rather than a recurring empirical series, and a conditional on disapproval following enactment would merely restate the clause. This provision honestly has no forecastable metrics, series hints, stance matrices, or conditionals.
goals: Disapprove the EPA final rule cited at 89 Fed. Reg. 73293 so that it has no force or effect.

effects.mechanism: Direct legal effect — already achieved by a related law
effects.text: The clause says that, if enacted, H.J. Res. 79 would disapprove the identified EPA rule and make it have no force or effect. Congress.gov separately records that the same disapproval was enacted through S.J. Res. 31 as Public Law 119-20 on June 20, 2025, so this House resolution does not identify a distinct additional regulatory outcome on the checked status date.
